attribution_text: NOAA / NWS Space Weather Prediction Center. Lumina presents bounded source values and provider notifications for educational information, not operational guidance.
authentication_method: The selected public NOAA SWPC JSON products require no Lumina credential or API key.
cache_ttl: Fresh for 10 minutes after a successful atomic five-product snapshot; stale-if-error for the following 50 minutes; expired thereafter.
contact_or_user_agent_requirement: Lumina sends a fixed identifying User-Agent without personal data. Requests use HTTPS, fixed GET paths, no query values, no redirects, and no inherited proxy environment.
failure_and_fallback_behaviour: Fetch the five approved products in order under one provider lease and one request-cycle deadline. Validate every component before atomically publishing one snapshot; on any failure retain the prior complete snapshot, quarantine only the failing bounded response when applicable, and expose stale data only during the approved stale-if-error interval.
fetch_time_policy: Each accepted snapshot records one Lumina retrieval time in the generic provider cache. Component source timestamps remain in their normalized fields and are not replaced by retrieval time.
fixture_and_checksum_strategy: Offline tests use sanitized deterministic fixtures for each of the five reviewed products, including quiet, active, malformed, missing, oversized, unsafe-text, retry, and partial-failure cases. Each exact component body is SHA-256 hashed and the ordered bodies receive the LUMINA-SWPC-SNAPSHOT-V1 framed aggregate SHA-256.
known_limitations: The v1 snapshot uses only the current NOAA scales record with source categories R, S, and G; it does not derive a scale from Kp or solar-wind measurements.
Kp rows preserve NOAA observed, estimated, and predicted statuses; Kp is a planetary index and is not a local aurora visibility prediction.
Solar-wind values are upstream or near-Earth spacecraft measurements and are not ground weather, local conditions, or an aurora probability.
Notifications are presented as the latest bounded SWPC notifications. Lumina does not infer active, cancelled, watch, warning, or alert state from message prose.
Aurora v1 is a fixed official NOAA Aurora 30-Minute Forecast link and model explanation only. Lumina does not ingest OVATION data or promise local visibility.
Lumina is educational and informational; operational users must consult NOAA / NWS SWPC directly.
observation_or_publication_time_policy: NOAA scale DateStamp and TimeStamp, Kp time_tag, and notification issue_datetime are retained as provider text under their reviewed source representations. Solar-wind time_tag values are retained as explicit UTC text. None is relabeled as browser-local time or as the Lumina retrieval time.
purpose: Bounded current NOAA / NWS Space Weather Prediction Center values for Lumina's educational Space Weather surface.
rate_or_fair_use_constraints: One logical provider lease and one circuit cover the finite five-request plan. Successful synchronization is scheduled every five minutes, with at most three attempts per failing component while the circuit is closed, deterministic one- and two-second retry spacing, provider-specific response bounds, and a 262144-byte complete raw evidence bound.
refresh_schedule: An external operator scheduler may enqueue provider.sync for noaa-swpc every five minutes using the canonical UTC five-minute idempotency bucket. The page and public API never trigger NOAA requests.
